findings.title: Peer reviewer identity is self-asserted rather than resolved to a trusted distinct principal
findings.evidence: The validator requires only a role string, a nonempty reviewer.identity string, and inequality with the source-owner role. It does not resolve that identity against a trusted reviewer registry, assigned review workflow, or other authentic source-bound peer record. The passing three-batch test supplies the unregistered literal peer-workflow-test-2, which satisfies the gate. The error says registered review principal, but no registration check is present.
findings.impact: Caller-authored peer JSON can claim PASS under a fabricated identity. The source semantics and row bindings may be correct, but the projector cannot establish that a distinct reviewer actually performed the review. This prevents treating a generated PASS record as genuine independent peer acceptance.
findings.repair: Resolve reviewer identity and review assignment from an authoritative peer workflow or registry; bind that trusted principal and its review record to the exact candidate bytes, source pins, and postimage hashes. Reject unregistered identities and candidate-author self-review.
findings.acceptanceCriterion: An arbitrary nonempty identity such as peer-workflow-test-2 is rejected unless a distinct, trusted workflow record resolves it and binds the exact candidate; a genuine registered reviewer remains accepted.
findings.predecessor: PDP0-BATCH-PEER-AUTHORITY-001 from the 2026-10-23 independent projector review remains unresolved for the distinct-peer half.
findings.nextAction: Repair peer identity resolution before relying on this projector to produce or consume a genuine peer PASS.

findings.title: Source-peer regression cases do not isolate their stated acceptance behavior
findings.evidence: The positive fixture is rejected before review validation because its case lacks the exact semanticBinding required by the hardened projector. The malformed-R4 batch is rejected by the hardened exact live-contract guard, but the test expects an obsolete error string. The forged-authority case also fails at that earlier semanticBinding guard, so it does not demonstrate rejection at the owner/peer workflow boundary.
findings.impact: The suite does not provide a passing source-backed positive control or an isolated forged-authority regression. The R4 malformed input is rejected in execution, but its assertion is stale. These failures reduce confidence in the claimed test coverage without negating the observed R6 source-content repairs.
findings.repair: Update the positive fixture to include exact live semantic bindings; assert malformed R4 rejection by behavior or the current guard message; make the forged-authority fixture otherwise semantically valid so the test reaches and exercises the authority gate.
findings.acceptanceCriterion: All three tests pass and prove, respectively, a valid live projection, rejection of malformed R4 cases, and rejection specifically at the owner/peer workflow validation stage.
